summary: Mildly frustrated Poseidon lacks main centre number
detailed_context: Scott is working through a task involving contacting someone at a St. Catharines location (likely related to the earlier discussion about Janet's test results and residential vs commercial determination). The question 'don't you have the main centre number for St.Catharines?' reveals mild frustration that Poseidon either didn't provide this information proactively or doesn't appear to have access to it. The phrasing indicates Scott expected this to be readily available—suggesting his mental model is that Poseidon should have access to public facility/centre contact information. The gap between expectation (you should know this) and apparent reality (you don't seem to) creates low-level dissatisfaction. This isn't anger, but rather disappointment in capability or responsiveness. Scott seems to want Poseidon to be more self-sufficient in retrieving practical contact details without requiring multiple manual requests.
